title: Trump Says No to Iran's Deal to Reopen a Key Waterway
summary:
Imagine a giant doorway on the ocean where about one out of every five barrels of oil in the world passes through. That doorway is called the Strait of Hormuz, between Iran and Oman. Since February, Iran has mostly kept it closed after the U.S. and Israel attacked Iran.

On Saturday, Iran made an offer: it would reopen the strait within seven days and restart talks about its nuclear program. In return, the U.S. would have to lift its naval blockade of Iranian ports, stop punishing countries that buy Iranian oil, and agree to a ceasefire (when both sides stop fighting for a while) that would include Lebanon.

President Donald Trump said no. "That deal would not be acceptable," he told reporters outside the White House. He said Iran is "losing so badly" that it wants a deal.

Iran's president, Masoud Pezeshkian, had just left New York after a big meeting of world leaders at the United Nations. He said Iran is still open to talking.

Also on Saturday, Saudi Arabia said it stopped a missile from Houthi fighters in Yemen. No one was hurt in that report, which hasn't been independently checked yet.
why_it_matters: When a key oil doorway on the ocean closes, fuel can cost more everywhere, which means buses, food deliveries, and family car trips can all get more expensive.
